channel.title: Harleen Kaur — Engineering notes
channel.description: Engineering decisions, experiments, and evidence for AI workloads.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 1: The Standard Renewal, End to End
item.description: The buyer accepts. Billing succeeds. Access fails. Explore four interactive workflows showing how a standard renewal qualifies, records consent, activates and recovers.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 2: When the Standard Path Ends
item.description: A shorter term and a new clause turn one renewal into several decisions. Explore commercial routing, versioned approvals and strategic procurement.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 3: Renewing a Commitment When Usage Changes
item.description: A precise shortfall projection can still rest on bad data. Follow reconciled usage through intervention, evidence review and commitment rightsizing.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 4: Retention Beyond the Renewal Date
item.description: Lower spend can mean better efficiency. Follow customer value, explicit cancellation decisions and verified reactivation across three interactive workflows.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 5: The Work After the Sale
item.description: The agreement is active, but the integration is blocked. Connect post-sale milestones, partner evidence and customer replies to owned outcomes.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 6: Follow the Money
item.description: A payment succeeds but its acknowledgement disappears. Explore reservations, reconciliation, refunds and exact-cent service allocation.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 7: Let Agents Work Within a Boundary
item.description: An agent can propose a plan without gaining permission to accept for the buyer. Explore provider boundaries, durable scheduling and execution-based evaluations.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 8: Forecast the Business from the Work
item.description: Preserve what the business believed last week. Explore operational forecasts, synthetic model evaluation and multi-cycle portfolio experiments.

item.title: Renewal Studio, Part 9: From Demonstration to an Operational System
item.description: Connect the hosted AWS demo to its source, identity and recovery boundaries, then define the evidence a narrowly scoped real pilot would need.

item.title: Improving Agents Starts with Verifying the Work
item.description: I compared reported completion with verified outputs in a live AutoHelix experiment. Inspect the results, scripted cheating controls, and limits of editing the improvement strategy.

item.title: Your AI remembers you. Can it remember a lie?
item.description: Follow a false approval across sessions, inspect 40 synthetic memory-authority episodes, and see why provenance and current permission need separate checks.

item.title: Testing subscription abuse at the action boundary
item.description: A synthetic subscription workflow compares permissions, business invariants, and deny-all controls, with recorded effects, explicit completion limits, and replayable evidence.

item.title: Designing an Evidence Trail for Agent Actions
item.description: I trace one synthetic agent action from its request to its observed effect, then examine what event hashes, snapshots, and replay can establish—and what needs additional verification.

item.title: When rules beat decision models
item.description: I replaced a label-matching diagnostic with an executable support workflow. On 144 synthetic test episodes, the rules baseline outperformed the tested zero-shot model configurations.
